plan.name: Read the decision journal in one GraphQL query
plan.summary: After a restart the dashboard read decisions/journal with one contents call per file, 122 of them, so its first refresh took 1 minute 42 seconds and every new decision added a call; now it reads the journal at the branch's newest commit in one GraphQL query. A new read in internal/github/read.go, Client.Files(ctx, dir, ref) ([]DirFile, error), asks GitHub through `gh api graphql`, with the query and its variables as fields and its answer decoded as MergeCommits does, for `query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $expression: String!) { repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) { object(expression: $expression) { ... on Tree { entries { name type oid object { ... on Blob { text isTruncated } } } } } } }` with the expression <ref>:<dir>, and returns each blob directly in the directory as a DirFile with its Name, its blob ID as OID and its Text, leaving out entries that aren't blobs, such as subdirectories; a directory that isn't there is ErrNotFound, and a blob whose text is truncated or null is an error, since its text can't be read whole. In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go, readJournal makes that one call for each new commit, with decisions/journal and the commit's SHA, in place of listing the commit's tree and reading each new file through the contents API, and as now it keeps only the files named *.jsonl, builds the graph again only when a file's blob ID changed or a file was added or removed, keeps the last good graph and lists the journal as stale when the read or the build fails, and reads nothing outside decisions/journal. The acceptance test #111's plan added, TestTheServerReadsAJournalFileAgainOnlyWhenItChanges, which counts one contents read per changed file, is removed from internal/dashboard/decisiongraph_accept_test.go with whatever only it uses, since these tests take its place, and internal/github/github_test.go gets unit tests of the new read. This changes the trusted base, internal/github, so a person merges it.

tests.name: TestARefreshReadsTheJournalInOneQuery
tests.says: With every journal file new, as after a restart, a refresh reads decisions/journal at the branch's newest commit in one GraphQL query, which asks for each entry's type and blob ID and each blob's text and whether it was truncated, for a journal of 3 files and of 40, and reads no file one at a time; the page's graph is the one built from the files read one at a time.

tests.name: TestACommitThatChangesNoJournalFileKeepsTheGraph
tests.says: When the branch moves to a commit that changes no journal file, the server reads nothing more than its one query there, and the page keeps its graph without building it again: the fake answers that commit with D-0002's text changed under the same blob ID, so a graph built again would differ.

tests.name: TestTheGraphFollowsTheJournalInOneQuery
tests.says: When the branch moves to a commit that changes a journal file, adds one and removes one, the server reads the journal there in one query, and the page's graph becomes the one built from that commit's files.

tests.name: TestAFailedJournalQueryKeepsTheLastGoodGraph
tests.says: When the query fails, or GitHub truncates a journal file's text, the page keeps the last graph that built and lists the journal as stale, and the next commit whose journal reads whole brings the graph up to date.
